runs.name: ITOCHU Corporation
runs.entry: Price **¥2,155** (TSE 8001 close 2026-10-09; Tokyo shut 2026-10-12) and ADS **$13.62** (close 2026-10-12; USD/JPY 158.56), all aggregator, flagged; **1 ADS = 1 share** on the depositaries' post-split F-6 POS amendments (Citibank 0001193805-26-000004, JPMorgan 0001193805-25-001740, Deutsche Bank 0001104659-26-002352; which of the four unsponsored programmes trades as ITOCY not stated in any filing read) x **6,899,334,417 shares** (7,924,447,520 issued less 931,394,253 treasury at 2026-06-30, Q1 results of 2026-08-06, less 93,718,850 bought back to 2026-09-30 per the disclosure of 2026-10-01; five-for-one split 2026-01-01, all figures post-split) = cap **¥14,868bn** ($93.8bn); sovereign **4.136%** (JGB 30Y, Ministry of Finance jgbcme.csv, 2026-10-08). Not an SEC registrant: `tools/run.py` and `cover_shares.py` returned nothing; every figure by hand from the company's own documents (Financial Information Reports FY2022 to FY2026, annual-report financial sections FY2016 to FY2021, Integrated Report 2025, FY2026 and Q1 results, the 2026 convocation notice, timely disclosures); operating cash flow FY2026 ¥1,131,837M cross-checked English against the Japanese 決算短信. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the company's annual documents, as the overnight brief directs. **Q1 IN** on the deciding part: no part carries half of five-year segment net profit (segment net profit is the only part measure filed, a CONVENTION of the run), so the largest decides, Metals & Minerals at 24.3% (¥1,020.9bn of ¥4,203.2bn, FY2022 to FY2026): 8% of BHP's Western Australia iron-ore joint ventures, 18.1% of CSN Mineração, some coking coal; profit from ¥(16.7)bn (FY2016) to ¥246.9bn (FY2023), ¥143.5bn FY2026; the company will not state its iron-ore price assumption ('N.A.'). The analyst read the unforecastable price as Q7's range width, not a Q1 refusal, and set down that the other reading closes at Q1 TOO HARD (NATURE). Cited M2012-065, M2009-059, M2011-084; M2023-031 weighed, not deciding. **Q2 IN**: the low-cost exception for a commodity, on BHP's own 20-F (0001193125-26-354647): the 'world's lowest cost major iron ore producer', US$19.66 a tonne, 62% margin; coal in turnaround. Q3 and Q6 weighed. **Q4 accounts IN, weighing against**: a featured 'core profit', a published profit plan, and a FY2015 reclassification of a coal investment that kept its ¥46.5bn FY2016 fall out of net profit, carried to Q5. **Q5 IN** (integrity; Okafuji chief executive since 2010, ability weighs for). **Q7 OUT on the floor**: owner cash (operating cash less net capital spending, lease repayments and minority dividends) five-year average **¥523.1bn all-equity**, ¥508.8bn equity-only (net profit averaged ¥840.6bn); net purchases of businesses ¥222.4bn a year; shown growth 10.86% capped (f) at sales growth 4.79%, above the JGB, so held at 4.136%; net debt ¥3,610bn. Value range **¥1,466 to ¥1,902 all-equity central ($9.25 to $12.00 per ADS)** against ¥2,155, equity-only ¥1,940 to ¥2,355; central cases earn 3.1% to 3.8% at the price, and the price is above the top. Fair price **¥289 all-equity ($1.82 per ADS)**, ¥789 equity-only ($4.97); the signed unclosed Dentsu Soken purchase (about ¥215bn) beside, ¥31 a share off every figure. Q8 to Q12 not reached. Balance sheets FY2017 to FY2026: equity ¥2.40tn to ¥6.59tn (¥1.05tn of it translation), associates ¥1.63tn to ¥4.10tn, net debt to equity 0.97 to 0.46, about ¥1.1tn of leases from 2020. Recorded after the stop, not weighed: about ¥731bn lent to or invested in the vehicle holding 20% of CITIC against a look-through market value of ¥701bn; directors paid on consolidated net profit with no capital charge; buybacks name no price (¥1,813 tender, about ¥2,274 in the market); return on capital added since FY2022 about 3%. Competitors: the documents name none by name; no competitor row. Contamination declared by the analyst: VSXY commit subjects, other research-folder names and memory lines in its session context; an MITSY run named in the framework text; the company's own disclosure of 2026-03-02 that National Indemnity holds over 10%, seen on the IR news list; ledger rows L2023-008, M2023-031, M2025-018 on Berkshire's trading-house purchase weighed only as rows about named companies; nothing decided by them. Commits 91ec1b11 to 6ae1cd9c. Citations: the analyst's check 76 distinct ids present, no E-ids; the dispatcher's adjacency script (MTSUY's `dispatcher_check.py`) 46 adjacent fragments, 0 slips. Position note filled at the fold (not held). check_framework PASS. **For the operator: this run and the MTSUY run of the same day split on the same question.** MTSUY closed TOO HARD (NATURE) at Q1 on a commodity-priced deciding part; ITOCY passed Q1 on a commodity-priced deciding part by reading the price as Q7's. The analyst's gaps: (1) whether an unforecastable product price is a Q1 matter or a Q7 matter (a ruling would make the two runs agree); (2) the parts threshold where only segment net profit is filed, and whether an unallocated 'Others' holding CITIC is a part; (3) IFRS 16 leases against Q7's finance/operating split; (4) whether the no-growth case carries purchases (this run carried none, raising the bottom); (5) the cap's degenerate case when sales growth exceeds the JGB; (6) whether minority buy-outs (¥450bn of the window) are purchases of businesses (shown without them: range ¥1,466 to ¥2,033, fair ¥338); (7) dividends on fair-valued holdings inside operating cash.
runs.narr: Q7 OUT on the floor: a Japanese trading house in nine parts where none has half the profit, so Metals & Minerals decides at 24.3%; IN at Q1 and Q2 on BHP's lowest-cost Western Australian iron ore, the analyst reading the unforecastable ore price as Q7's range width (the MTSUY run of the same day read the same question as a Q1 stop; the operator's ruling is owed). Range ¥1,466 to ¥1,902 all-equity at the 4.136% JGB against ¥2,155 (3.1% to 3.8% at the price); fair ¥289 all-equity ($1.82 per ADS), ¥789 equity-only. Against: CITIC carried above its look-through value, pay on net profit with no capital charge, buybacks with no price limit.
